title: Kainos has the workbook's strongest public-sector access: 15 lots across 8 CCS frameworks
content:
Kainos is approved on 15 lots across 8 Crown Commercial Service frameworks, which the workbook records as the strongest documented public-sector access it holds on any firm. The wording matters: this is evidenced access, upgraded from the assumption that a large UK supplier probably has framework coverage, to a counted position on named frameworks.

The offsetting finding is that its anchor is Workday — it is described as Europe's largest boutique Workday partner, alongside Microsoft and AWS credentials including Premier MSP status and 500-plus certified engineers. That anchoring dilutes custom-build purity: a practice organised around configuring a proprietary SaaS suite is a different delivery motion from bespoke, client-owned systems, and it is the SaaS vendor that owns the system of record in those engagements.

The row stays at priority 9 despite the best access in the corpus, and that inversion is the transferable lesson. Access to public buyers is necessary but not sufficient; the screen weights partnership fit above route-to-market, the same way it does for the Sopra Steria entries. Framework coverage tells you a firm can sell into government, not that it would sell this.
